lede: All six extensions are scored. Class labels hold on Fashion. PatchGAN digits is one glyph with a high pixel std.
title: Conditional GAN and the other two variants
question: Does a class label, a PatchGAN discriminator, or feature matching change quality and diversity?
process: ConditionalGenerator concatenates the noise with an embedding of the class label before the MLP. The MLP discriminator concatenates the same embedding with the image. PatchDiscriminator concatenates a one-hot map to the image and scores patches. The generator and discriminator losses stay the binary cross-entropy above, now conditioned on the label.
Feature matching adds one term inside _generator_terms. It is an L1 distance between the mean discriminator feature of the fake batch and the mean feature of the real batch, with weight 10:

DATASET in 01_get_data.py swaps digits and Fashion. model_selection.py then calls the same train and eval functions. Only the variant name and the output folder change. The six runs, 250 images per class, all have spread ratios between 0.88 and 1.12. PatchGAN digits still repeats one glyph.

opening.summary: The bar is sample std divided by real std. Vanilla sits near 0.04 and 0.08. The six conditional runs sit between 0.88 and 1.12. The class grid is the part the ratio hides.
opening.hover: Hover a bar to open that class grid.

marks.label: vanilla digits
marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: Vanilla digits, from the earlier run: sample std 0.0134 / real std 0.378 = 0.035. mode_collapse is true. One repeated stroke. The class-conditional runs below are the same training code with a label.

marks.label: vanilla fashion
marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: Vanilla Fashion: 0.0413 / 0.531 = 0.078. mode_collapse is true. One shirt.

marks.label: cGAN digits
marks.summary: cGAN digits: sample std 0.6362 / real std 0.6074 = 1.05. mode_collapse is false. Diversity 0.630, class separation 0.636. Each row is a different digit. Sharpness is 0.628 against real 0.256, so the ink is speckled. Generator loss equals BCE at 2.074, so this run has no feature-matching term. Eval D is 0.216.
marks.frameCaption: cGAN digits. One class per row.

marks.label: cGAN fashion
marks.summary: cGAN Fashion: 0.6140 / 0.6468 = 0.95. mode_collapse is false. Diversity 0.560, class separation 0.600. Rows separate into shirts, trousers, shoes, and bags, and they are speckled. Sharpness 0.698 against real 0.301. Eval D 0.665, generator loss 3.257, equal to BCE.
marks.frameCaption: cGAN Fashion. Rows follow garment classes.

marks.label: PatchGAN digits
marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: PatchGAN digits: 0.5365 / 0.6074 = 0.88, so mode_collapse is false and the ratio looks healthy. The class grid is still one binary glyph on every row. Pixel std stays high because that glyph is high-contrast and jitters. The label did not change the picture. Diversity 0.537, class separation 0.537, sharpness 0.393 against real 0.256. Eval D 0.611, generator loss 2.814, equal to BCE.
marks.hover: ratio 0.88, and every class row is the same glyph
marks.frameCaption: PatchGAN digits. One glyph in every class row.

marks.label: PatchGAN fashion
marks.summary: PatchGAN Fashion: 0.7122 / 0.6468 = 1.10. mode_collapse is false. The class grid does change with the label: shirts, trousers, coats, sandals, bags, and shoes are different rows, and they read as garments more clearly than the speckled cGAN. Diversity 0.675, class separation 0.637, sharpness 0.427 against real 0.301. Eval D 1.075, generator loss 1.030.
marks.frameCaption: PatchGAN Fashion. Class rows are different clothes.

marks.label: FM digits
marks.summary: Feature matching on digits: 0.5624 / 0.6074 = 0.93. mode_collapse is false. The class rows are different digits, still speckled. Diversity 0.554, class separation 0.561, sharpness 0.471 against real 0.256, closer to real ink than the cGAN's 0.628. Generator loss is 6.539 and BCE is 2.976, so the feature-matching term is in the objective. Eval D is 0.449.
marks.frameCaption: Feature matching, digits. Class rows differ.

marks.label: FM fashion
marks.answers: Why do you think the results might not be great?
marks.summary: Feature matching on Fashion: 0.7266 / 0.6468 = 1.12. mode_collapse is false and diversity is 0.656, the high end of this table. The class grid is less readable than PatchGAN Fashion: several rows are speckled blobs, and a few still suggest a shirt, a sandal, or a bag. Sharpness 0.672 against real 0.301. Generator loss 7.411 against BCE 2.706. The extra term is active, and it did not buy a cleaner garment.
marks.frameCaption: Feature matching, Fashion. High spread, speckled rows.

reflection.worked: Measured: six archives finished 40 epochs with history, scores, class grids, and a model. Digits and Fashion share the training loop; only load_data and the variant folder change. Class labels stop the vanilla collapse. PatchGAN Fashion rows are different clothes. Feature matching on digits moves sharpness from the cGAN’s 0.628 toward real ink, to 0.471.
reflection.unexpected: Measured: PatchGAN digits has spread ratio 0.88 and mode_collapse false, and every class row is the same glyph. Feature matching on Fashion has high diversity and speckled rows. The mirrored best_params.json records only the cGAN variant.
reflection.why: Measured: the collapse flag fires only under a ratio of 0.2. Guess: a PatchGAN on a thin stroke collapses to one glyph that is still high-contrast, while the same discriminator keeps a wide garment silhouette.
reflection.improve: Read the class grid next to the ratio. On digits, keep the cGAN or feature matching. On Fashion, train PatchGAN longer. Compare generator BCE across variants, and leave the feature-matching term on its own axis.
